content.text:
I fixed `addMonths` in `dates.js`. Jan 31 plus 1 month now gives Feb 28 instead of rolling over into March. The existing tests pass.

JavaScript's `setMonth` was the cause. Adding a month to the 31st of a month that has 31 days overflowed into the next month, so those customers were billed a month late. The function now moves to day 1, shifts the month, then sets the day to the original day or the new month's last day, whichever is smaller.

I ran a few cases by hand, all keeping the 10:30 time of day:
- Jan 31 2026 + 1 gives Feb 28 2026.
- Jan 31 2024 + 1 gives Feb 29 2024, a leap year.
- Mar 31 2026 − 1 gives Feb 28 2026.
- Jan 31 2026 + 13 gives Feb 28 2027.
- Jan 15 2026 + 1 gives Feb 15 2026, so ordinary dates are unchanged.

The input date is still copied, never changed.
